OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is
            assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits.
            The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the '+'; the stored value is
            that E.164 string.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid email address; the stored value is lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. When omitted on create it
            defaults to the server's current date. Serialized as an ISO date
            'YYYY-MM-DD'.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even if another owner already
            has the same last name and address (they share a household). A
            request-only flag; it is not stored or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3
                is the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN is
                a global 4-digit zero-padded sequence assigned at creation time.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable shared identifier for owners who belong to the same
                household (same last name and address). Assigned when an owner is
                created with sharesHousehold true; every owner in that household
                carries the same value. Null when the owner is not part of a
                shared household.
              type: string
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F6'
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:
      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object
      properties:
        content:
          title: Content
          description: Pet owners in the requested page.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Owner'

## Summary

I implemented `namesakeCount` on `POST /api/owners` — the number of existing owners sharing the same first and last name (case-insensitively) at creation time, snapshotted and returned on reads.

**Changes:**

1. **`CountNamesakes.java`** (new function) — iterates existing owners via `OwnerRepository.findAll()` and counts those matching the new owner's first+last name case-insensitively (trimmed/lower-cased), then stores the count on the owner. It runs *before* save, so the new owner isn't counted. Modeled on the existing `AssignCustomerCode` step.

2. **`owners.POST.yml`** — wired `countNamesakes` into the pipeline after `assignHousehold` and before `save`, under the same `transaction` governance.

3. **`Owner.java`** — added a persisted `Integer namesakeCount` field (`@Column(name = "namesake_count")`) with getter/setter, so the value is stored and read back by `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

4. **Schema SQL** (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres) — added the `namesake_count` column to the `owners` table.

5. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `namesakeCount` integer property to the `Owner` schema; MapStruct maps it automatically onto the generated `OwnerDto` (same field name).

The test creates two owners named "Ann" with the same surname (different postcodes to avoid the household-duplicate 409), then confirms the second owner's `namesakeCount` is `1`.
